findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/delivery-promise-outcome.ts:61-106 and packages/main/src/tasks/delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts:378-409 — HIGH: the accepted delivery table is materially weaker than CHK-001. For explicit status=met/verified, the normalizer synthesizes verifiedBy=status:<value> and never requires evidence, so incomplete explicit PASS rows are persisted and pass both machine/DONE consumers. status=waived rejects verifiedBy but accepts evidence, and status=unverified accepts evidence; the checklist explicitly requires met/verified without required claims plus waived/unverified verification claims to be contradictions before persistence. The smoke institutionalizes the bug by listing status=met with no verifiedBy/evidence as passing and omits waived+evidence / unverified+evidence from invalidRows. Remove synthesized certification, define the exact accepted table (explicit met/verified require the promised non-empty claims; waived/unverified reject every incompatible verification field), and generate the matrix from that table so writer and readers share a correct predicate rather than the same false PASS.

packages/main/src/tasks/production-test-seam-guard.ts:66-84,178-181 — HIGH: sanitizer recognition is text-presence based, not return/data-flow based. Any function whose body merely contains Number(...), Number.isFinite(...), >0, and Math.floor(...) is globally trusted; expressionSources then erases all argument taint for calls to it. Repro on the built analyzer: function fakePositiveInt(raw){ const n=Number(raw); Number.isFinite(n); if(n>0)Math.floor(n); return raw; } writeFileSync(fakePositiveInt(process.env.TEST_TARGET), owned) returns [] issues. This lets an env-derived arbitrary filesystem/process value bypass the new production guard without a file allowlist, so CHK-002 edge:0/adversarial coverage does not close the F-011 class. Require structural proof that every returned value is the bounded parsed/fallback or finite fixed enum, and add this deceptive-sanitizer negative fixture.

The new production test-seam guard is bypassable through ordinary local data flow, so it does not enforce the advertised no environment-controlled side-effect invariant. analyzeProductionTestSeams only propagates taint into function parameters and simple identifier assignments; CallExpression returns only union(argument sources), and property assignments are ignored. A minimal executable repro against the built analyzer reports [] for both `function target(){ return process.env.TEST_FILE; } writeFileSync(target(), "x")` and `const x={}; x.path=process.env.TEST_FILE; writeFileSync(x.path, "x")`, while the direct form is detected. Production core/handler code can therefore reintroduce an arbitrary TEST/SMOKE-selected filesystem/process target and keep this guard green. Track return-value/property data flow (or use a conservative AST rule that rejects any TEST/SMOKE env source in production side-effect code), and add these bypasses plus process-sink equivalents as self-tests.
